approach: Since the wall is smooth, the floor alone carries the ladder's full weight, so the maximum friction at the floor is the coefficient of friction times that weight.

steps.text: The wall is smooth, so it pushes only sideways on the ladder and supplies no vertical support. The floor must therefore carry the ladder's entire weight vertically.
steps.equation: N (floor, vertical) = weight of ladder = 250 N

steps.text: The maximum friction force the floor can supply is the coefficient of friction times this normal force.

common_mistakes.text: Misreading the ladder's weight of 250 N as a mass of 250 kg and multiplying by g again gives f_max = 0.3 × 250 × 10 = 750 N.
